# My Thinking

I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over forty years. My father farmed it before me. I know this soil, I know this climate. We get maybe 500 millimeters of rain a year, most of it in July and August, and the aquifer is still there if I pump for it.

I will grow winter wheat and summer maize, same as always. The wheat goes in the ground in October, comes out in June, then I seed maize right after without wasting a day. Same rotation my neighbors use, same rotation the extension station has pushed for thirty years. The guaranteed purchase price for grain means I'm not gambling on markets I don't understand.

I have about 8 mu. All of it goes into this rotation — I'm 66 and my knees are not what they were. Vegetables would need me to be in the field every day, and cotton needs too much hand labor. Wheat and maize I can mostly manage with my small tractor and my son helping during harvest.

For wheat, I'll use the improved variety from the county seed station — I've been planting "Kenong 199" the last few years, it handles the rust well. Three irrigations: one in early winter to help it overwinter, one at jointing, one at heading. I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting and chase it with urea at jointing. Two or three sprays — one herbicide in winter, one fungicide when the flag leaf comes out.

For maize, I buy hybrid seed — "Zhengdan 958," it's reliable, everybody uses it. I'll drill it straight into the stubble, no plowing, saves time and diesel. Two irrigations if the rains fail. One herbicide spray after emergence, one for corn borer if I see the damage.

I don't experiment anymore. At my age, a bad harvest is not something I can recover from easily.
